quick.summary: Why finding mismatches at the end of a sprint is too late, and the habit that fixes it.
quick.takeaway: Review the build while it is half done.

beats.line: I saw the built feature on the last sprint day. Ten things were off. Too late?
Too late to fix calmly. When did you last look before that?
Then small gaps grew for two weeks.

board.text: review at the end = ten fixes

beats.line: Ask to see it half built. Ten minutes, at their desk or on a call.
Won’t developers feel I’m checking up on them?
Ask what is unclear in your design. Then it is help, not inspection.
Can I see it on Wednesday, and tell me what my file left unclear?
Two small fixes midweek, none on the last day.

quiz.question: When is the best time for a designer to review a feature being built?
options: While it is partly built, so gaps are cheap to fix
On the last day of the sprint
Once testing has signed it off
quiz.explanation: Early reviews catch small mismatches before more work is built on top of them.

quiz.question: Reviewing a build early usually means fewer fixes at the end of the sprint.
quiz.explanation: Gaps found while work is in progress are quick to correct; found at the end, they pile up.
